item.title: Hundreds of Utah students walk out of class to protest ICE actions
item.description: High school students across the Salt Lake Valley walked out of class on Tuesday, raising their voices in protest against the actions of ICE.

item.title: Federal Reserve keeps interest rates unchanged even as Trump continues to insist they be lowered
item.description: The Federal Reserve pushed the pause button on its interest rate cuts Wednesday, leaving its key rate unchanged at about 3.6% after lowering it three times last year.

item.title: Utah lawmaker wants to nearly triple the state’s minimum wage; require pay transparency in job listings
item.description: If passed, a new bill would raise Utah's minimum wage from $7.25 an hour to $20 an hour.

item.title: South Salt Lake Police officer trainee arrested on suspicion of DUI
item.description: A police officer in training with the South Salt Lake Police Department was booked into jail Sunday after allegedly being under the influence of alcohol while on duty.

item.title: Amazon cuts about 16,000 corporate jobs in the latest round of layoffs
item.description: Amazon is cutting about 16,000 jobs in the latest round of tech industry layoffs. Beth Galetti, a senior vice president, announced this Wednesday in a blog post. The reductions follow October's layoffs of 14,000 workers.

item.title: University of Utah professor finds that ship fuel emissions might not impact climate change
item.description: A University of Utah professor has found that reduced ship fuel emissions may not increase global warming, contrary to what some scientists theorized.

item.title: Two companies supplied dried milk powder linked to botulism in ByHeart baby formula
item.description: Two suppliers provided dried milk powder that could be linked to the outbreak of botulism in ByHeart formula that has sickened dozens of babies.

item.title: Sarah Mullally confirmed as archbishop of Canterbury, first woman to lead the Church of England
item.description: The Confirmation of Election service for Sarah Mullally, archbishop of Canterbury, marks a major milestone for the Church of England, which ordained its first female priests in 1994 and its first female bishop in 2015.

item.title: Bomb threat at U of U verified as hoax, increased police presence to remain overnight
item.description: SALT LAKE CITY — Police at the University of Utah have verified that a campus bomb threat received just after 4 p.m. was a hoax. “Lockdowns at University Hospital and Primary Children’s Hospital will be lifted,” police said in their update. item.title: Republicans fear their midterm chances are slipping away over immigration chaos
item.description: Republicans are increasingly worried about immigration enforcement becoming a political problem in the upcoming midterm elections.
